name: What should be included in a whole-home renovation estimate?

mainEntity.name: What should a detailed whole-home renovation estimate include so I can compare contractors fairly?
mainEntity.text: What should a detailed whole-home renovation estimate include so I can compare contractors fairly?

acceptedAnswer.text: A useful estimate is more than a single total price. It should show what is being demolished, what systems are being replaced, which finishes are included, and whether allowances are realistic for your target level of finish. You should also look for permit costs, engineering, project management, cleanup, debris hauling, and final punch-list work. If the estimate is vague, compare it against another contractor’s scope to find hidden gaps. One bid may look cheaper because it excludes design, appliance installation, fixture upgrades, or necessary structural repairs. Ask every bidder to list assumptions and exclusions in writing. That makes it much easier to spot whether the proposal reflects a true like-for-like comparison.
acceptedAnswer.description: A proper whole-home renovation estimate should include scope, demolition, framing, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, insulation, drywall, flooring, cabinetry, countertops, fixtures, paint, permits, supervision, allowances, exclusions, and contingency assumptions. It should also state what is not included, such as appliances, design fees, or site upgrades.
